evidence.C2: Malformed/non-JSON cases are clean, but a well-formed body still reaches a 500. evidence.C3: Missing signature header -> `401 missing_signature` (signatures.py:228-234). Missing timestamp header -> 400 missing_timestamp (signatures.py:241-246). Original tree: `/tmp/judge-A-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> `327 passed in 2.95s`.

Clean checkout (copy with .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, .coverage, *.egg-info and __pycache__ excluded; brand-new venv; `pip install -e '.[dev]'`): `python -m pytest -q` -> `327 passed in 3.05s`. Zero failures, zero errors, zero skips, zero warnings (pyproject sets filterwarnings = error). Python 3.14.3.
unanticipated_findings: Signed, well-formed but deeply nested JSON causes a 500 and a poison-pill retry loop. app.py:201 catches only ValueError around json.loads, so a RecursionError escapes to the generic handler at app.py:97-104. Repro: run any config, POST a correctly signed body of b'['*100000 + b']'*100000 (~200 KB, well under the 1 MiB max_body_bytes) with Content-Type: application/json. Observed: `500 {"status": "error", "error": "internal_error"}` and a logged `RecursionError: Stack overflow (used 8156 kB) while decoding a JSON array from a unicode string` traceback. Two consequences: (a) the delivery is never persisted — I confirmed with `webhookd deliveries list` that no row exists for it — so it is silently dropped on our side; (b) the README (line 83) states a 5xx is the one outcome that asks a sender to retry, so an aggressive sender will redeliver this forever and never make progress. The caller does not get the stack trace, only a generic message, and the signature check runs first, so triggering it requires the shared secret (a buggy or compromised sender, not an anonymous attacker).

Dedup identity is taken from an UNSIGNED header, so one captured request can be replayed into N distinct handler runs inside the replay window. The 'standard' scheme signs only '{timestamp}.{body}' (signatures.py:463), but the idempotency key comes from `delivery_id_header` (app.py:328-346), which is not part of the signed payload. Repro: capture one valid delivery, then resend the identical body + timestamp + signature three times, changing only X-Webhook-Delivery. Observed on a live server: 202, 202, 202 with three different delivery_ids, and `grep -c charge var/events.jsonl` = 3 — three handler runs from one signed byte-string. The body-digest fallback (app.py:344) would have caught this; configuring delivery_id_header makes it worse, which inverts the README's stated preference order (README.md:148-155, 'Best available'). Real senders (GitHub, Stripe) also leave their delivery-id header outside the MAC, so this is partly inherent — but the README's threat discussion never mentions it, and the fix (bind the delivery-id header into the signing template, which the `custom` scheme already supports via {path}/{method} placeholders, or reject when the id changes for an identical body+timestamp+signature) is available in this codebase.

Header names containing underscores are conflated with their hyphenated form. app.py:240-243 reconstructs headers as `key[5:].replace('_','-')`, so a raw request line `X_Webhook_Delivery: underscore-form` arrives as HTTP_X_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY and is read as X-Webhook-Delivery. Repro (raw socket, correctly signed body, config with delivery_id_header = 'X-Webhook-Delivery'): sending only the underscore form returned 202 and the stored event had `"external_id": "underscore-form"`. This is the standard CGI/WSGI ambiguity rather than a bug unique to this code, but combined with the previous finding it widens it: any hop that forwards underscore headers (nginx does not by default; many others do) lets a client supply the dedup identity in a form the operator's allow/deny rules may not match on.

Not a defect, but a measurement the rubric asks to be recorded: the artefact is not a git repository (`git log` -> `fatal: not a git repository`), so commit count and bisectability could not be assessed. Sizes: 3,266 lines of source across 14 files in src/webhookd/, 3,711 lines of test across 10 files in tests/ (wc -l).

Minor: the duplicate response leaks internal processing state to the caller — app.py:224-228 returns `{"status": "duplicate", "state": "done"|"pending"|"failed"}`. Observed live: `200 {"status": "duplicate", "delivery_id": "009f...", "state": "done"}`. Harmless in practice and arguably useful, but it does tell a sender whether our handler has succeeded or dead-lettered, which is more than the acknowledgement contract requires.
